project.name: muninn-website
project.description: A React 18 and Vite public news reader with story, Events, and administrative review interfaces. It consumes Current_news artifacts generated by the Muninn backend publishing workflow and uses AWS Amplify.

tour.title: Product Context and Entry
tour.description: Start with Muninn's current product vocabulary and repository operating rules, rather than the legacy template README, then follow the main entry point into the running application. Together these stops distinguish Topics, Situations, Events, Developments, and Reports, establish the public UI and data boundaries, and show where Amplify, diagnostics, and React first enter the runtime.

tour.title: Runtime Route Selection
tour.description: Continuing from the bootstrap in Step 1, App selects the public reader or authenticated editorial route and conditionally adds beta feedback. The generated AWS exports supply the cloud identifiers that make authentication and backend selection possible.
tour.languageLesson: React StrictMode deliberately exercises development behavior more aggressively, while a top-level route selector keeps authentication and experience selection outside the feature views themselves.

tour.title: Public Reader Architecture
tour.description: Building on the route selection from Step 2, ReaderApp coordinates Muninn's Today, story, Event, coverage, archive, weekly Letter, and personalized-news surfaces. LegacyHome contains the established Today and Events discovery experience, including taxonomy and user-state behavior, so these two broad modules reveal most of the public product's navigation and data flow.
tour.languageLesson: Large React feature components often combine route state, effects, derived data, and rendering; their high fan-out makes them useful architectural maps but also signals natural future decomposition seams.

tour.title: Personalization Workflows
tour.description: The public reader delegates focused preference tasks to accessible modal workflows for news-section ordering, newsletter setup, and smaller customization choices. Together they normalize user input before handing it back to the broader reader and cloud-backed state mechanisms introduced later.
tour.languageLesson: Controlled React forms keep draft values in component state and emit a normalized payload on save, while Escape and backdrop handlers make modal state changes accessible and predictable.

tour.title: Weekly Letter Experience
tour.description: WeeklyLetter extends the reader with published and preview newsletter artifacts, preserving internal links, editorial sections, images, and related coverage. A dedicated preview entry point mounts the same experience independently, which lets editorial preview remain separate without duplicating the feature implementation.

tour.title: Editorial Review and Feedback
tour.description: The authenticated editorial console turns review candidates, timelines, digest clusters, quality signals, and beta reports into an operational workflow. BetaReporter complements it on the reader side by collecting structured descriptions and visual evidence, closing the loop between public experience and editorial diagnosis.

tour.title: Diagnostics and Persistence
tour.description: The feedback path from Step 6 is supported by privacy-sanitized browser diagnostics and a persistence layer that can use Amplify GraphQL plus private storage. A bounded local fallback keeps previews useful when cloud services are unavailable, while evidence retrieval helpers support the reviewer experience.

tour.title: Amplify Data Contract
tour.description: The GraphQL schema defines the durable contract behind personalization and beta reporting, including owner-scoped UserState and role-aware BetaIssue records. Its authorization directives make access control part of the data model, connecting the authenticated routes and evidence workflows from the previous steps to AppSync, Cognito, DynamoDB, and storage resources.
tour.languageLesson: GraphQL schemas define API contracts at the type level, while Amplify authorization directives attach owner, IAM, identity-pool, and group access rules directly to models and operations.

tour.title: Generated Client Bindings
tour.description: Generated TypeScript models and query or mutation documents translate the schema from Step 8 into strongly typed client operations. The generated Amplify configuration binds those operations to the deployed AppSync, Cognito, and S3 resources, so these files should be regenerated from the contract rather than treated as independent business logic.
tour.languageLesson: Generated GraphQL documents preserve operation shapes and TypeScript result types together, reducing drift between React data handling and the deployed schema.

tour.title: Responsive Design System
tour.description: The reader and editorial features share several CSS layers: broad application primitives, the full reader presentation system, and the redesigned public shell and cards. Their responsive rules also encode important product decisions around image cropping, Today hierarchy, Events discovery, administration, and mobile behavior.

tour.title: Compatibility and Content Inputs
tour.description: Legacy-compatible story and newsletter pages preserve older links and provide fallback rendering while directing modern identifiers into the React reader. The digest synchronization utility shows the other side of that boundary: published JSON is an input to the website, not frontend implementation source.
tour.languageLesson: Compatibility pages can preserve stable public URLs during a framework migration, while separating generated content artifacts from application source prevents automated publishing from overwriting implementation code.

tour.title: Build and Deployment
tour.description: The package manifest and Vite configuration define local commands plus separate main and weekly-preview build entries. Production can then follow either the Amplify Hosting pipeline or the GitHub Pages workflow, both of which build the same Vite application into a deployable dist artifact.
tour.languageLesson: Vite supports multiple HTML entry points through Rollup input configuration, while CI YAML separates triggers, jobs, and sequential build steps so deployment remains reproducible.
